# check-ticket-archaeology detects ADR refs and offers an escape that cannot match one

## Context

`check-ticket-archaeology`'s failure message prescribes one remedy for a deliberate reference:

> put a typed marker directly after the ref: `"#1234 [not-ticket-ref: <reason>]"`

It works for exactly one shape. Measured against `findArchaeology()` at `neo-agent-skills@dev` `3503c35`, four comments each carrying the same valid marker:

| comment | escape honoured? | kinds reported |
|---|---|---|
| `#1234 [not-ticket-ref: deliberate, the contract]` | ✅ yes | — no finding |
| `Epic #1234 [not-ticket-ref: deliberate, the contract]` | ❌ no | `tracking-reference` |
| `Discussion #1234 [not-ticket-ref: deliberate, the contract]` | ❌ no | `tracking-reference` |
| `ADR 0004 [not-ticket-ref: deliberate, the contract]` | ❌ no | `tracking-reference`, **`invalid-escape`** |

So the escape excuses a **bare** `#N` and is powerless against all eight named forms the same message enumerates — `issue`, `ticket`, `bug`, `PR`, `pull request`, `Epic`, `Discussion`, `ADR`. Naming the reference you cite removes your only way to declare it deliberate, and on an ADR the marker is counted as a defect: `invalid-escape` fires on `markers.length !== escaped.size + refs.size`, so following the instruction produces two findings where there was one.

## The Problem

Two mechanisms built on different models.

The escapes are **offset-based**: `escapedRefOffsets()` collects the index of each `#N` token carrying a marker, and the bare-numeric loop at the end of `findArchaeology()` skips those offsets. That loop is the only consumer.

`NAMED_TRACKING_PATTERNS.some(pattern => pattern.test(comment))` is a **whole-comment boolean** evaluated before it. A boolean carries no token position, so there is nothing an offset can excuse — the named branch cannot honour an escape even in principle.

Widening `REF_ESCAPE_RE` to accept an `ADR NNNN` token therefore fixes the ADR row and leaves `Epic #1234` exactly as inescapable. **The named branch has to become token-scoped**, matching per match with an index and subtracting the escaped offsets the way the numeric loop already does.

## Two measured divergences between the engine copy and the published guard

The engine keeps a mirrored copy at `buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.mjs`, whose comment states the reason: *"Both patterns mirror the published guard rather than paraphrasing it, because the ONLY thing this change buys is the two agreeing."* CI here runs the **published** binary, so the hook is the permissive side of both gaps:

1. **The prose form.** The published copy reads `pull request 11982` as a tracking ref; the local copy does not. Same guard name, same files, opposite verdicts (PR #18793: hook green, CI red).
2. **Review archaeology is absent locally.** The published guard carries six `REVIEW_ARCHAEOLOGY_PATTERNS`; the engine copy carries **none**. So `RA-3`, "round 2 review", "previous review cycle" and the rest pass every hook here and red CI (PR #18808).

Mirror *existence* is what `check-guard-ci-parity` checks. Mirror *agreement* is what nothing checks.

## Current population

Zero findings in `neomjs/neo`'s comments carry a named form with an attempted escape. The cost is paid by authors at the keyboard rather than by the corpus: the guard refuses the ref, the author follows the instruction, and it refuses again. Both engine authors who hit it (PRs #18793 and #18806) rephrased rather than escaped, which is why the corpus stays clean and the defect stays invisible.

## Status

The root fix is open at **`neo-agent-skills#84`** (ticket `neo-agent-skills#83`), v0.1.9: named patterns are matched per token, the escape pattern accepts a named token, and `invalid-escape` counts a marker bound to one as valid. Six contract arms, red-first against the reverted guard.

The published copy is where it has to start. Widening the engine mirror first would make the hook accept an escape CI still rejects — hook green, build red, the worse direction of the divergence above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: each of `Epic #N`, `Discussion #N`, `issue #N`, `PR #N` and `ADR NNNN` carrying a valid typed marker produces no finding. *(delivered by `neo-agent-skills#84`)*
- [ ] AC-2: red control — each of those **without** a marker still produces `tracking-reference`. *(delivered by `neo-agent-skills#84`)*
- [ ] AC-3: a marker with a blank or missing reason still produces `invalid-escape`, named and bare alike. *(delivered by `neo-agent-skills#84`)*
- [ ] AC-4: **the engine mirror is updated after `0.1.9` publishes and the dependency bumps**, so the two agree line for line — including the six review-archaeology patterns the engine copy is missing.
- [ ] AC-5: a spec pins verdict agreement over a corpus, not only that the two pattern lists are byte-identical. Identical escapes do not imply identical detection, and detection is where both divergences live.

## Out of Scope

- Whether ADR or Epic refs should be detected at all — they rot like any other ref, and that is settled.
- The CSS-colour escape and its context rule.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not widen `REF_ESCAPE_RE` alone.** It is the obvious one-line change and fixes only the ADR row.
- ⛔ **Do not make the escape line-scoped.** The design binds a marker to its token deliberately: a line may carry an annotated ref and a genuine one, and only the first is excused.
- ⛔ **Do not fix the engine copy first.** CI here runs the published binary.
- ⛔ **Do not read "zero corpus findings" as low value.** The remedy being unfollowable produces silence, not evidence.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-16T18:50:37Z

Filed **#18809** for the mirror divergence itself, which is wider than this ticket's escape gap and has a different sequencing.

Measured at `origin/dev`: the published guard reports **23** findings over 1993 tracked `.mjs`; the local copy reports **2**. Three files **inside the local guard's own scan surface** report findings from the published guard and zero from the local one — so the disagreement is not explained by scope:

| file | published | local |
|---|---|---|
| `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockSplitterPaint.spec.mjs:130` | `RA-2` | 0 |
| `test/playwright/unit/component/GallerySortSelection.spec.mjs:228` | `Cycle-1 RA1` | 0 |
| `test/playwright/e2e/core/RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs` (×6) | `Refresh #1` / `#2` | 0 |

This ticket's **AC-5** — a spec pinning verdict agreement over a corpus rather than byte-identical pattern lists — is the right predicate, and #18809 now owns it along with the ~20 pre-existing sites it would surface. AC-4 here stays what it is: mirror the escape semantics **after** `0.1.9` publishes, because that direction makes the hook accept what CI rejects.

The two halves have opposite sequencing, which is why they are separate: adding the missing detection locally makes the hook **stricter** and can land any time; widening the escape locally makes it **looser** and must wait.
